notes:
I couldn't write the Isaiah 57 notes, because I wasn't able to read any of the source pages.

I tried to open six pages at once: Enduring Word, Ellicott, Gill, Pulpit Commentary, Matthew Henry on StudyLight, and the NET Bible notes. The pages came back in a format my script didn't expect, and it crashed before saving or showing any text. Then my research tool hit its usage limit for this turn, so I couldn't retry.

You asked me to report only what the pages actually say and to give a URL for every point. Without having read any of them, I can't write a single note that meets those rules, so I've left the notes out rather than fill them from memory.

If you send a new message, I can start again. I'd read the sources one or two at a time so one bad page can't stop the rest. The order would be:

1. **Traditional reading, verse by verse:** Enduring Word, the Ellicott, Gill and Pulpit Commentary pages on Bible Hub, and Precept Austin.
2. **Where Protestant traditions differ:** mainly v. 15 (God living with the humble and contrite), v. 19 ("peace to those far and near," which Ephesians 2:17 picks up) and vv. 1–2 (the righteous dying and finding rest). I'd look at Wesley's notes, Gill and Spurgeon, Ligonier or The Gospel Coalition, and Lutheran sources.
3. **Other views:** the NET Bible notes on the hard Hebrew in vv. 6, 8 and 9 (the smooth stones, the "memorial" and Molech), Bible Odyssey on child sacrifice and Molech, and Catholic or Orthodox readings if those sites cover the chapter.
